passages.title: The Dance of the Honeybee
passages.text: When a honeybee finds a rich patch of flowers, it returns to the hive and performs a 'waggle dance' to share the news. The direction of the straight run in the dance, measured against the vertical of the honeycomb, shows the angle between the food and the sun. The length of the run tells how far the flowers are: the longer the waggle, the greater the distance. Other bees follow the dancer closely, touching her with their antennae, and then fly out to find the food. The Austrian scientist Karl von Frisch spent decades decoding this behaviour and was awarded a Nobel Prize in 1973. Some people once believed that insects were merely simple machines, but the waggle dance suggests a remarkably sophisticated system of communication. Even so, scientists remain cautious. They say that the dance is a message, not a language, because bees cannot use it to talk about anything except food and nesting sites.

passages.title: The Village Well
passages.text:
Before the sun has climbed the hill,
The women gather, grave and still;
Their brass pots ring, the ropes run dry,
And gossip rises to the sky.
The well is old; its stones are worn
By hands that came before the morn.
It gives to all, it asks no fee,
It keeps each secret faithfully.
But now the pipes are laid in rows,
And water through the tap now flows;
The well stands silent, mossed and deep,
A grandmother lost in endless sleep.
Yet children, passing, drop a stone
And listen for its distant tone,
As if the dark were still a friend
Who answers those who stop and bend.

passages.title: Let the Library Door Stay Open
passages.text: The municipal library in our town, which has served three generations of readers, will reduce its opening hours from next month. The authorities blame a shortage of funds and say that most people now read on their phones. This argument is, at best, half true. A phone may carry a thousand books, but it cannot give a poor student a quiet table, a working fan and a librarian who knows which book to hand over next. Nor is the saving significant: the cut will save less than the corporation spends on its annual inaugurations. A library is not a luxury to be trimmed when budgets tighten; it is the cheapest school a town can build. We urge the corporation to reconsider before the shutters come down on a habit that took decades to grow and may take far longer to restore.

questions.question: Choose the correct simple sentence for: "As soon as the thief saw the police, he ran away."
options: The thief ran away as seeing the police.
Seen the police, the thief ran away.
On seeing the police, the thief ran away.
The police seeing, the thief ran away.
questions.explanation: A complex sentence with 'As soon as' is reduced to a simple sentence with 'On + -ing'. 'On seeing the police, the thief ran away' is the only grammatical option; the others are ungrammatical.

questions.question: Change into indirect speech: She said to him, "Do you know the answer?"
options: She asked him that he knew the answer.
She asked him if he knew the answer.
She told him if he knows the answer.
She asked him did he know the answer.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question in indirect speech is introduced by "if/whether" with assertive word order and the tense shifts back: "if he knew the answer".

questions.question: It was in 1947 ____ India became independent.
questions.explanation: In a cleft sentence "It was ... that ..." the relative word "that" is used to focus on the time; "what", "whom" and "whose" do not fit.

questions.question: Unless you hurry, you ____ the bus.
questions.explanation: "Unless" means "if not". The first conditional uses present simple in the clause with "unless" and "will" in the main clause: "will miss".

questions.question: Which is the correct elliptical form of: "He wanted to go, but I did not want to go."?
options: He wanted to go, but I didn't want.
He wanted to go, but I didn't.
He wanted to go, but I didn't to.
He wanted to go, but didn't I.
questions.explanation: The repeated words 'want to go' can be omitted after the auxiliary 'didn't'. Options A and C leave incomplete verb phrases and D has wrong word order.

questions.question: Choose the correct determiner: He has ____ friends, so he often feels lonely.
questions.explanation: 'Few' (almost none) has a negative sense that fits 'lonely' and is used with countable plural nouns. 'A few' is positive; 'little' and 'a little' are for uncountable nouns.

questions.question: When I was young, I ____ run very fast.
questions.explanation: "Could" expresses past ability. "Can" is present, "shall" and "must" do not express past ability.

questions.question: He seldom goes to the temple, ____?
questions.explanation: "Seldom" has a negative sense, so the main clause is treated as negative and the tag must be positive: "does he?".

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The cricket match had to be ____ because of heavy rain.
questions.explanation: 'Call off' means to cancel. 'Call in' means to summon, 'call up' means to telephone or recruit, and 'call on' means to visit.

questions.question: Mathematics ____ my favourite subject.
questions.explanation: Names of subjects ending in -s (Mathematics, Physics, Economics) take a singular verb, so "is".

questions.question: I ____ my homework when the teacher entered the room.
questions.explanation: A longer past action interrupted by a shorter past action uses the past continuous: "was doing".

questions.question: Identify the underlined clause: The book (that you lent me) is very interesting.
questions.explanation: 'That you lent me' modifies 'book' and is essential to identify which book is meant; it has no commas. So it is a defining relative clause.

questions.question: Change into a complex sentence: "He worked hard, so he passed."
options: Because he worked hard, he passed.
Though he worked hard, he passed.
He passed so that he worked hard.
If he worked hard, he passed.
questions.explanation: 'So' shows result; in the complex form the cause becomes a subordinate clause with 'because'. 'Though' shows contrast, and the others change the meaning.

questions.question: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "The earth moves round the sun."
options: The teacher said that the earth moved round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth had moved round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth was moving round the sun.
questions.explanation: A universal truth keeps the present tense in indirect speech, even after a past reporting verb. The other options wrongly backshift the tense.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Not only ____ the examination, but he also topped it.
questions.explanation: When a sentence begins with 'Not only', the auxiliary comes before the subject (inversion): 'did he pass'. The other word orders are incorrect.

questions.question: The prefix 'mis-' in words like 'misunderstand' and 'misspell' means:
questions.explanation: The prefix 'mis-' means wrongly or badly.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The ship was held up at the ____ for two days.
questions.explanation: A 'pier' is a platform built out into water where ships stop. 'Pear' is a fruit, 'peer' means to look closely or an equal, and 'pair' means two.

questions.question: In which sentence does the word 'light' mean 'not heavy'?
questions.explanation: Only in 'a light bag' does 'light' mean of little weight. In the others it refers to illumination or a signal.

questions.question: Choose the correct collocation: She ____ a mistake in the last question.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'make a mistake'. 'Do', 'take' and 'give' are not used with 'mistake'.

questions.question: Choose the correct collocation: There was ____ rain throughout the night.
questions.explanation: 'Heavy rain' is the natural collocation. 'Strong rain', 'big rain' and 'tall rain' are not used.

questions.question: Choose the correct adjective form of the noun 'danger'.
questions.explanation: The suffix -ous forms the adjective 'dangerous'. The other forms do not exist in standard English.

questions.question: In the sentence 'I will book a ticket for you', the word 'book' is used as a ______.
questions.explanation: 'Book' here means 'reserve' and follows the modal 'will', so it is a verb, though it is usually a noun.

questions.question: Complete the common lexical bundle: "____ the other hand, he is quite honest."
questions.explanation: 'On the other hand' is a fixed expression used to introduce a contrast.

questions.question: Complete the lexical bundle: "In the ____ run, honesty pays."
questions.explanation: "In the long run" means over a long period of time or in the end.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'under the weather' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Under the weather' means feeling slightly unwell.

questions.question: What is meant by 'a white elephant'?
options: A costly possession that is of little use
questions.explanation: A "white elephant" is a possession that is costly to keep but of little use or value.

questions.question: The idiom 'a piece of cake' means:
questions.explanation: 'A piece of cake' means something that is very easy to do.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech: "All hands on deck!" (the captain calls the sailors)
questions.explanation: A part ("hands") stands for the whole (sailors), which is synecdoche.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech: "He is as brave as a lion."
questions.explanation: A direct comparison using 'as ... as' is a simile. A metaphor would say 'He is a lion'.

questions.question: "Parting is such sweet sorrow." The figure of speech used here is:
questions.explanation: 'Sweet sorrow' combines two contradictory words in one phrase, which is an oxymoron.

questions.question: According to the passage, the length of the waggle run indicates:
questions.explanation: The passage says 'the longer the waggle, the greater the distance'. The others are not mentioned.

questions.question: Scientists call the dance 'a message, not a language' because:
options: it conveys information only about food and nesting sites
it is too slow to follow
it is performed by only one bee in a hive
questions.explanation: The last sentence states bees cannot use it to talk about anything except food and nesting sites. The passage says nothing about speed, a single dancer or lack of rules.

questions.question: The word 'sophisticated' in the passage is closest in meaning to:
questions.explanation: 'Remarkably sophisticated system' means a highly developed, complex system, so 'advanced' fits best. It is the opposite of 'simple'.

questions.question: The tone of the author in the passage is:
questions.explanation: The author explains facts and ends with the scientists' cautious view. There is no sarcasm, humour or anger.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT supported by the passage?
options: Bees touch the dancer with their antennae.
The dance shows the angle between the food and the sun.
Von Frisch worked for many years to decode the dance.
The dance can describe any topic to other bees.
questions.explanation: The passage says the dance can only talk about food and nesting sites, so D is not supported. A, B and C are all stated.

questions.question: The rhyme scheme of the first four lines of the poem (hill, still, dry, sky) is:
questions.explanation: hill/still rhyme and dry/sky rhyme, so the pattern is AABB (rhyming couplets).

questions.question: "A grandmother lost in endless sleep" is an example of:
questions.explanation: The well is directly described as a grandmother without 'like' or 'as', which makes it a metaphor.

questions.question: "It keeps each secret faithfully" suggests that the well:
options: is a trusted listener of people's private talk
questions.explanation: The women's gossip and confidences were shared at the well, which 'kept' them. Line 7 says it 'asks no fee', so D is wrong.

questions.question: The mood of the poem towards the end is:
questions.explanation: The poet recalls the past with gentle sadness, and the children's stone-dropping keeps a memory alive. This is a nostalgic, wistful mood.

questions.question: What has replaced the well as the source of water in the village?
questions.explanation: The poem says 'the pipes are laid in rows, and water through the tap now flows'.

questions.question: According to the editorial, the cut in library hours will save less than the corporation spends on its annual:
questions.explanation: The passage says the saving is less than the corporation spends on its annual inaugurations.

questions.question: The phrase 'at best, half true' implies that the authorities' argument is:
questions.explanation: 'Half true' means there is some truth (people do read on phones), but the argument ignores what a library offers.

questions.question: "The cheapest school a town can build" is an example of:
questions.explanation: The library is described as a school without a word like 'like' or 'as', so it is a metaphor.

questions.question: 'Before the shutters come down' in the passage means:
questions.explanation: Shutters coming down is a figure for closing a place of business. Here it refers to the library closing.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the editorial as something a library gives a poor student?
options: A librarian who knows which book to hand over
questions.explanation: The editorial mentions a quiet table, a working fan and a knowledgeable librarian. Free internet access is not mentioned.

questions.question: Total Physical Response (TPR), developed by James Asher, mainly connects language learning with:
questions.questionHi: टोटल फिजिकल रिस्पॉन्स (TPR) विधि, जिसे जेम्स आशर ने विकसित किया, भाषा सीखने को मुख्यतः किससे जोड़ती है?
options: physical actions in response to commands
optionsHi: आदेशों के प्रत्युत्तर में शारीरिक क्रियाएँ
questions.explanation: In TPR learners listen to commands and respond with body movements, which makes comprehension come before speaking.
questions.explanationHi: TPR में विद्यार्थी आदेश सुनकर शारीरिक क्रिया करते हैं, इसलिए बोलने से पहले समझ विकसित होती है।

questions.question: The concept of 'interlanguage' was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Larry Selinker (1972) coined 'interlanguage' for the learner's developing in-between language system. Skinner, Krashen and Bruner are associated with other ideas.
questions.explanationHi: लैरी सेलिंकर (1972) ने सीखने वाले की विकसित हो रही मध्यवर्ती भाषा के लिए 'interlanguage' शब्द दिया। स्किनर, क्रेशन और ब्रूनर अन्य विचारों से जुड़े हैं।

questions.question: In a multilingual classroom, the best use of learners' home languages is to:
questions.questionHi: बहुभाषी कक्षा में बच्चों की घरेलू भाषाओं का सबसे अच्छा उपयोग क्या है?
options: use them as a bridge to learn English
optionsHi: केवल अंग्रेज़ी पाठ्यपुस्तक का उपयोग करना
अंग्रेज़ी सीखने के लिए उन्हें सेतु की तरह उपयोग करना
उनका प्रयोग करने वाले बच्चों को दंड देना
questions.explanation: Home languages are a resource; using them helps understanding and builds new learning on prior knowledge. Banning or punishing harms confidence.
questions.explanationHi: घरेलू भाषाएँ एक संसाधन हैं; इनसे समझ बढ़ती है और पूर्व ज्ञान पर नया ज्ञान बनता है। प्रतिबंध या दंड से आत्मविश्वास घटता है।

questions.question: The first step in remedial teaching is to:
questions.questionHi: उपचारात्मक शिक्षण (remedial teaching) का पहला चरण है:
options: repeat the same lesson to the whole class
optionsHi: सीखने की विशेष कठिनाई का निदान करना
पूरी कक्षा को वही पाठ दोहराना
questions.explanation: Remedial work must begin with diagnosis so that teaching targets the real difficulty. The other options do not address the cause.
questions.explanationHi: उपचारात्मक कार्य निदान से शुरू होना चाहिए ताकि शिक्षण वास्तविक कठिनाई पर केंद्रित हो। अन्य विकल्प कारण को नहीं सुलझाते।

questions.question: Suggestopedia, developed by Georgi Lozanov, tries to lower learners' anxiety by using:
questions.questionHi: जॉर्जी लोज़ानोव द्वारा विकसित सजेस्टोपीडिया विधि विद्यार्थियों की चिंता कम करने के लिए किसका उपयोग करती है?
options: relaxation, music and a comfortable environment
questions.explanation: Suggestopedia uses music, relaxation and a pleasant classroom to reduce stress and help learning.
questions.explanationHi: सजेस्टोपीडिया में संगीत, विश्राम और सुखद कक्षा द्वारा तनाव कम कर सीखने में सहायता दी जाती है।

questions.question: Which view of language learning is associated with Skinner's behaviourism?
questions.questionHi: भाषा सीखने का कौन-सा दृष्टिकोण स्किनर के व्यवहारवाद से जुड़ा है?
options: Learning through social interaction in the ZPD
Habit formation through stimulus, response and reinforcement
optionsHi: ZPD में सामाजिक अंतःक्रिया से सीखना
उद्दीपन, अनुक्रिया और पुनर्बलन से आदत निर्माण
questions.explanation: Behaviourists see language as a habit built by imitation and reinforcement. A is Chomsky's view and B is Vygotsky's.
questions.explanationHi: व्यवहारवादी भाषा को अनुकरण और पुनर्बलन से बनी आदत मानते हैं। A चॉम्स्की का और B वाइगोत्स्की का दृष्टिकोण है।

questions.question: In Chomsky's theory, 'LAD' stands for:
questions.questionHi: चॉम्स्की के सिद्धांत में 'LAD' का अर्थ है:
questions.explanation: LAD is the innate mental faculty that enables children to acquire language. The other expansions are invented.
questions.explanationHi: LAD वह जन्मजात मानसिक क्षमता है जिससे बच्चे भाषा अर्जित करते हैं। अन्य विस्तार गढ़े हुए हैं।

questions.question: The study of the structure and formation of words is called:
questions.questionHi: शब्दों की बनावट और निर्माण के अध्ययन को कहते हैं:
questions.explanation: Morphology studies words and their parts (morphemes). Phonology deals with sounds, syntax with sentence structure and pragmatics with language in use.
questions.explanationHi: Morphology शब्दों और उनके अंशों (morphemes) का अध्ययन है। Phonology ध्वनियों, syntax वाक्य संरचना और pragmatics भाषा के प्रयोग से संबंधित है।

questions.question: Phonics is a method of teaching reading by linking:
questions.questionHi: फोनिक्स (phonics) पढ़ना सिखाने की वह विधि है जो किसे जोड़ती है?
optionsHi: शब्दों को मातृभाषा के अर्थ से
questions.explanation: Phonics teaches the relationship between sounds (phonemes) and the letters that represent them.
questions.explanationHi: फोनिक्स ध्वनियों (phonemes) और उन्हें दर्शाने वाले अक्षरों के संबंध को सिखाता है।

questions.question: Which activity is best for developing speaking skill in a primary class?
questions.questionHi: प्राथमिक कक्षा में बोलने का कौशल विकसित करने के लिए सबसे अच्छी गतिविधि कौन-सी है?
questions.explanation: Role play and pair talk give real speaking practice. The other activities mainly involve writing or silent reading.
questions.explanationHi: भूमिका-अभिनय और जोड़ी में बातचीत से वास्तविक बोलने का अभ्यास मिलता है। अन्य गतिविधियाँ मुख्यतः लिखने या मौन पढ़ने की हैं।

questions.question: Teaching grammar 'inductively' means:
questions.questionHi: व्याकरण को 'आगमनात्मक' (inductive) ढंग से पढ़ाने का अर्थ है:
options: giving rules first and then examples
letting learners observe examples and discover the rule
optionsHi: पहले नियम देना और फिर उदाहरण
बच्चों को उदाहरण देखकर स्वयं नियम खोजने देना
questions.explanation: In the inductive approach learners move from examples to the rule. Giving the rule first is the deductive approach.
questions.explanationHi: आगमनात्मक विधि में बच्चे उदाहरणों से नियम की ओर जाते हैं। पहले नियम बताना निगमनात्मक (deductive) विधि है।

questions.question: The Grammar-Translation Method mainly emphasises:
questions.questionHi: व्याकरण-अनुवाद विधि मुख्यतः किस पर बल देती है?
questions.explanation: This method teaches through rules, vocabulary lists and translation, giving little attention to speaking.
questions.explanationHi: यह विधि नियमों, शब्द-सूचियों और अनुवाद से पढ़ाती है तथा बोलने पर कम ध्यान देती है।

questions.question: Dyslexia is a learning difficulty mainly related to:
questions.questionHi: डिस्लेक्सिया मुख्यतः किससे संबंधित अधिगम कठिनाई है?
questions.explanation: Dyslexia is a difficulty in reading and decoding words despite normal intelligence.
questions.explanationHi: डिस्लेक्सिया सामान्य बुद्धि के बावजूद पढ़ने और शब्दों को पहचानने की कठिनाई है।

questions.question: Difficulty in handwriting and written expression is called:
questions.questionHi: हस्तलेखन और लिखित अभिव्यक्ति की कठिनाई को क्या कहते हैं?
questions.explanation: Dysgraphia affects writing; dyscalculia affects mathematics and dyslexia affects reading.
questions.explanationHi: डिस्ग्राफिया लेखन को, डिस्कैल्कुलिया गणित को और डिस्लेक्सिया पढ़ने को प्रभावित करता है।

questions.question: A child says "goed" instead of "went". This is an example of:
questions.questionHi: एक बच्चा "went" की जगह "goed" कहता है। यह किसका उदाहरण है?
questions.explanation: The child applies the regular "-ed" rule to an irregular verb; this is overgeneralisation.
questions.explanationHi: बच्चा नियमित "-ed" नियम को अनियमित क्रिया पर लगा देता है; यह अतिसामान्यीकरण है।
